# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — the hands. My view shows nothing yet: no wire states, no display, no light. I can't see anything printed or coloured, and I have no information from anyone yet.

Since I go second in the round (Mute, then me, then Deaf), I should have received the Mute's message already — but the context is empty, so either the Mute sent nothing or it hasn't reached me. I have nothing to report about the bomb yet.

My best move now is to wait and let the others send me what they perceive. I have no wire states to act on, and acting blind would detonate the bomb. I'll hold.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb reads: display shows the number 1. Indicator light is green. Seven wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. That is everything I can see.

Deaf has given me the full visual picture: display = 1, light = green, and the wire colours in order (1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue).

But I'm the Blind monkey — I can't see colours, and more importantly, the actual decision rules for this bomb live in the Mute's manual. Deaf's colours and display are useful context, but I must not act on them alone. The Mute reads the manual and knows the rule for "display 1 + green light" and which wire to cut based on colour.

I need the Mute's instruction. The Mute speaks before me in the order, but I haven't received anything from the Mute this round. I should send what I can to the Mute — the Mute can hear me — and give them the visual data that Deaf just gave me, since the Mute cannot see the bomb and may not have gotten Deaf's message (Deaf comes after me in the round, so Deaf's message reaches the Mute next round, not this one).

So: I'll speak to the Mute, relaying Deaf's visual reading, and ask for the rule/instruction. I won't act yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have Deaf's visual reading of the bomb: display shows 1, indicator light is green, and seven wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. I cannot see any of this myself and I cannot read your manual. Please tell me the rule for display 1 with a green light, and exactly which wire position to cut. I will not act until you tell me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. I received a gesture from Mute that I cannot decode yet, so I will not relay it to Blind. Mute, can you hear me? I will speak the code so you can use it. Proposal: to name a wire, gesture that many fingers: 1=?, 2=?, 3=?, 4=?, 5=?, 6=?, 7=?. To say cut, add ? after the number. To say do not cut, add ?. Blind: I will speak any wire instruction to you in words once Mute confirms.

Deaf is trying to set up a gesture code, but I never receive gestures — only speech. Deaf seems confused about who can perceive what. Deaf's gestures go to... actually, Deaf gestures are seen by whoever can see; I'm Blind, so I never receive gestures. And Deaf can't hear, so I can only reach Deaf via gesture, which Deaf can see. Mute can both hear me (speech) and see my gestures.

The key problem: I need the Mute's rule. The Mute speaks before me, but I've received nothing from Mute in words. Deaf received a gesture from Mute but can't decode it.

I should clarify the channel situation and push for the rule. I can speak to Mute (they hear me). I can also gesture to Deaf and Mute (both can see gestures), but Deaf can't hear and I can't hear gestures either — so Deaf and I can only communicate one-way: I gesture, Deaf sees; Deaf speaks, I hear. That works: Deaf speaks to me, I gesture to Deaf.

Let me gesture to Deaf to confirm I can see nothing and need the rule in words, and speak to Mute asking directly for the rule.

Actually, let me be efficient. The critical missing piece is the Mute's manual rule. Let me speak to Mute again, clearly, and gesture to Deaf to confirm the channel.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I still have no rule from you. I cannot read your manual and cannot see the bomb. Please just tell me in words: for display 1 with green light, which wire position do I cut? Reply with a single number 1 to 7.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute's gesture decodes as: cut wire number 5. Wire 5 is green. Blind, that is the instruction from the manual-reader. Do not cut yet. Mute, confirm with ? if wire 5 is correct. Also, Blind, your gesture read as 7 then 5 with no cut marker — what did you mean? I will not relay anything to Blind as a cut order until Mute confirms.

Now I have a rule candidate: cut wire 5 (green). Deaf decoded Mute's gesture as "cut wire 5." Deaf wants Mute to confirm.

My gesture of 👌✋ read as 7 then 5 to Deaf — that was accidental noise; I meant "OK/acknowledge." I should clarify that to Deaf so it isn't mistaken for an instruction.

The instruction "cut wire 5" makes sense: display 1, green light, wire 5 is green. Plausible rule (e.g., "display 1 + green → cut the green wire"). But I should get a clear confirmation from Mute before acting, since a wrong cut kills us all.

Let me speak to Mute to confirm, and gesture to Deaf to clarify my earlier gesture was just an acknowledgment, not an instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf decoded your gesture as: cut wire 5. Please confirm in words to me: is the instruction to cut wire 5? Answer yes or no, and if no, give the correct number 1 to 7.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed by both Mute and me. Cut wire number 5. It is the fifth wire in the row, between the orange wire (fourth) and the purple wire (sixth). Count from the left end: red, white, yellow, orange, then green — that green fifth wire is the one to cut.

Both Mute and Deaf now agree: cut wire 5, the green one, fifth from the left. The rule (display 1, green light) points to the green wire, and both channels confirm it. I'm the hands; this is my action to take.

I'll cut position 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New state after the correct cut. Wire 5 is cut. Display now shows the number 4. Indicator light is now blue. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Mute, the bomb changed — your previous instruction is spent. Give the next instruction for display 4, blue light.

The cut was correct — wire 5 is now cut, and the bomb advanced. New state: display = 4, light = blue, remaining wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue.

Now I need the Mute's rule for display 4 with a blue light. I'll relay the new state to Mute (who can't see) and ask for the next wire number. I'll also gesture to Deaf to acknowledge.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. The cut worked. New bomb state from Deaf: display shows 4, indicator light is blue. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Wire 5 is cut and gone. Please give the rule for display 4 with blue light: which wire position do I cut? Reply with a single number from 1,2,3,4,6,7.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute says cut wire number 3. It is the third wire from the left: red first, white second, then yellow third — cut that yellow wire. It sits between the white wire and the orange wire.

Mute says cut wire 3 (yellow). Deaf confirms the position: third from the left, between white and orange. I'll cut position 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
